body.estimand_functional: \((\widehat\theta,\widehat\tau_R)=(\widehat y(\widehat M)_r^+\widehat B,\ q^\top\{\widehat s_1-\widehat y(\widehat M)_r^+\widehat B\})\), with root-\(K\) influence \((\Phi_{\theta},\Phi_\tau)\)

sampling_model.design: A fixed set of target-pre, donor-pre, donor-post, and target factual-post cells is observed; treatment histories and grid times are fixed.
sampling_model.units: Each cell contains \(K\) independent individuals, and cell samples are mutually independent.
sampling_model.treatment: The target switches treatment after the pre period while donor units remain under control. The observed-law functional is \(\theta=yM_r^+B\); exact post-transport is the substantive equality \(\theta^{0}=\theta\) with the target's causal untreated post-period survival row (and hence \(\tau_R^{0}=\tau_R\)). Target-pre row membership is not needed by the joint limit theorem.
sampling_model.overlap: Conditional censor survival is at least \(g>0\) through every required cell horizon.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold cross-fitting estimates conditional event and censor survival. The positive theorem is conditional on \(a_K\to0\), \(b_K\to0\), \(a_Kb_K=o(K^{-1/2})\), origin normalization, a strictly positive true and fitted event-survival tail, bounded variation of \(R_{cf}\), and \(\max_{c,f,\ell}\|V_{cf\ell}(X)\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\). The tail and last two conditions are substantive learner restrictions, not consequences of generic machine-learning consistency. On a fixed finite support for covariates and event times, clipped empirical conditional hazard ratios and their finite product integral attain the learner-side conditions with \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\); any consistent censor learner with \(b_K=o(1)\) then satisfies the product rate. This finite-stratum certificate is not asserted for generic learners or for the TCL application.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) impose event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, use a fixed-grid latent-factor/PCR transport, and form the spectral inputs from marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves; they do not derive covariate-adjusted AIPCW spectral influence inference.
Published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4) gives asymptotic linearity for a directly estimated cross-fitted doubly robust treatment-specific survival curve.
Theorem 2 and Corollary 2 give row-space out-of-sample prediction guarantees for minimum-norm principal component regression.
Equation (4.12) gives the Fr\'echet derivative of the Moore--Penrose inverse under locally constant rank.
Sections 3--4 show interpolation, variance, and survival-curve bias for synthetic survival individuals.
Theorem 3.1 gives feasible inference for low-rank linear functionals when the working rank overestimates the true rank.

Theorem 2.1 recovers the factor space for bounded working rank at least the true rank as the cross-sectional dimension grows, and Theorem 3.2 with Corollary 3.1 gives over-estimated-rank-robust factor-augmented inference.

body.tldr: For fixed donor count, pre grid, post grid, rank, and a separated nonzero singular spectrum, covariate-adjusted cross-fitted AIPCW cell estimates have a joint root-\(K\) expansion conditional on a positive survival tail and explicit bounded-variation and relative-variation restrictions for the selected event learner. A clipped empirical hazard learner satisfies the learner-side restrictions with \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\) on a fixed finite-stratum submodel, but this certificate is not a generic learner result and does not verify the TCL application. The spectral functional \(\theta=yM_r^+B\) is distinct from the causal untreated curve \(\theta^{0}\); exact post-transport is the substantive equality that identifies \(\theta^{0}=\theta\), and likewise \(\tau_R^{0}=\tau_R\). The full three-block spectral derivative yields a possibly singular joint Gaussian law; positive coordinate variances suffice for the simultaneous band and a positive grid-RMST variance suffices for scalar studentization. Weak-gap and selected-rank inference remains open.

project_justification.gap: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) already state event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, but their spectral workflow uses marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves and does not give a covariate-adjusted joint influence law. With heterogeneous covariates, conditional independence need not imply marginal independence, so those cell inputs can converge to distorted curves before PCR transport. Westling et al. (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4)) provide asymptotic-linearity theory for a directly estimated treatment-specific curve, not for a learned three-block spectral counterfactual.
project_justification.niche: With \(N_0,T_0,J,r\) fixed and \(K\to\infty\), covariate-standardized cell curves form a finite-dimensional semiparametric first stage and \(\theta=yM_r^+B\) is a smooth spectral functional on a separated-rank neighborhood. Exact post-transport, rather than the definition of \(\theta\), makes this functional the causal curve \(\theta^{0}\). The bridge requires the exact Stieltjes remainder under a disclosed positive-tail and learner-path variation restriction, a concrete submodel on which the learner-side restrictions are attainable, and all three terms of the pseudoinverse derivative.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the conditional-learner AIPCW cell expansion, a finite-stratum clipped-hazard attainability certificate, the joint transported Gaussian law with possibly singular covariance, a Gaussian-multiplier band under positive coordinate variances, and a studentized grid-RMST interval under positive variance for the declared scalar contrast. Under exact post-transport these observed-law conclusions target \((\theta^{0},\tau_R^{0})\). It also retains the explicit open-subclass Kaplan--Meier/PCR bias result and leaves weak-gap inference open.

body.related_work: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) supply the fixed-grid latent-factor survival panel, unit and time spans, PCR transport, and the 925-patient, 10-country TCL application. They assume event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, but use marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier inputs and do not derive a covariate-adjusted transported influence law. Proposition~\ref{prop:han-shah-fixed-grid-embedding} gives their algebraic span bridge. Here \(\theta=yM_r^+B\) is first an observed-law spectral functional; exact post-transport is the separate causal equality \(\theta^{0}=\theta\), and the joint limit does not need target-pre row membership. Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4) and Sections 5.2--5.3) supply direct-curve cross-fitted augmented survival inference. The relative-survival variation restriction here is an additional primitive sufficient condition not imposed by Westling et al., who instead assume the exact Stieltjes-remainder rate. Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-stratum-hazard-certificate} proves that restriction for a fixed finite-stratum clipped empirical hazard learner, not for generic learners. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025, Theorem 2 and Corollary 2) study minimum-norm PCR and row-space prediction without censoring-aware asymptotics. Golub and Pereyra (1973, equation (4.12)) provide the constant-rank pseudoinverse differential. Curth, Poon, Nori, and Gonz\'alez (2024, Sections 3--4) analyze survival synthetic-control bias but not this three-block PCR pseudo-limit. Fan and Liao (2022) study growing-panel factor models, and Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2026) study robustness to rank misspecification. These are neighboring problems; weak-gap and selected-rank inference for the unregularized fixed-donor target remains an acknowledged open frontier of this note.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theory is fixed-dimensional and conditional on a strictly positive event-survival tail and on an event learner whose relative-survival path has the stated bounded variation and \(L_2\) variation rate. Ordinary supremum or \(L_2\) consistency does not imply those properties. The finite-stratum hazard certificate establishes attainability only for fixed covariate and event-time supports with uniformly positive at-risk probabilities, event hazards bounded away from one, and proportional training samples; it does not verify the restriction for generic learners or for the TCL data. The joint Gaussian covariance may be singular, but the band excludes zero counterfactual coordinate variances and the grid-RMST interval excludes zero variance in its scalar direction. The theory does not cover growing grids or panels, a shrinking singular gap, selected rank, approximate post-transport, or continuous-time RMST.
body.honest_scope: The joint cell expansion is a conditional-learner theorem under within-cell i.i.d. sampling, cross-cell independence for stacking, conditional independent censoring, censor positivity, fixed-fold nuisance consistency and product rate, origin normalization, a strictly positive true and fitted event-survival tail, and explicit bounded-variation and relative-variation restrictions. A concrete clipped empirical hazard learner discharges the learner-side restrictions with root-\(K\) rate only on the stated fixed finite-stratum submodel; this does not establish generic learner attainability or verify the 925-patient TCL application. The spectral limit additionally requires fixed panel dimensions, exact rank, a fixed singular gap, and exact post-transport: \(\theta=yM_r^+B\) and \(\tau_R=q^\top(s_1-\theta)\) are observed-law functionals, while that assumption supplies \(\theta^{0}=\theta\) and \(\tau_R^{0}=\tau_R\) as the causal-identification equalities. Target-pre row membership remains only in the Han--Shah embedding and converse uses. The joint covariance may be singular. The simultaneous band requires positive counterfactual marginal variances, and the studentized grid-RMST interval separately requires positive variance of \(q^\top(\Phi_1-\Phi_\theta)\). Applying either conclusion to TCL requires independent verification of all sampling, learner, transport, and relevant variance conditions. Nothing here covers growing dimensions, weak gaps, selected rank, approximate transport, or continuous-time RMST. Weak-gap inference remains the acknowledged follow-on question because its frontier also depends on weak loadings and a uniform triangular experiment, not only on \(\sigma_r(M_K)\).
